# my-ui-catalog — Full AI Context

## 1. Overview

`@noemaru1011/ui` is a reusable UI component library built with React and TypeScript.

It provides components for application interfaces, layout composition, common interactions, and low-level UI primitives.

Repository:

- https://github.com/noemaru1011/my-ui-catalog

Storybook:

- https://noemaru1011.github.io/my-ui-catalog/

npm package:

- `@noemaru1011/ui`

## 2. Technology Stack

The project uses the following technologies:

- React 19
- TypeScript
- Vite
- Tailwind CSS 4
- Base UI
- class-variance-authority
- i18next
- react-i18next
- Storybook

Use the package's published peer dependency requirements as the source of truth for compatibility.

## 3. Installation

```bash
npm install @noemaru1011/ui
```

Import the stylesheet in the application entry point:

```tsx
import '@noemaru1011/ui/style.css';
```

The stylesheet provides the library's Tailwind CSS output, theme variables, and component styles.

## 4. Public API

The package entry point is `src/index.ts`.

### 4.1 Elements

The Elements collection provides higher-level, reusable interface components.

```tsx
import {
  Accordion,
  Blockquote,
  Checkbox,
  Combobox,
  ComboboxMultiple,
  DatePicker,
  DateRange,
  DescriptionList,
  Disclosure,
  FileUpload,
  FileUploadButton,
  HamburgerMenu,
  Heading,
  Image,
  Input,
  PasswordInput,
  Link,
  List,
  Loading,
  Radio,
  LanguageSelect,
  Select,
  Switch,
  ThemeSwitch,
  Text,
  Textarea,
} from '@noemaru1011/ui';
```

Available components:

- Accordion
- Blockquote
- Checkbox
- Combobox
- ComboboxMultiple
- DatePicker
- DateRange
- DescriptionList
- Disclosure
- FileUpload
- FileUploadButton
- HamburgerMenu
- Heading
- Image
- Input
- PasswordInput
- Link
- List
- Loading
- Radio
- LanguageSelect
- Select
- Switch
- ThemeSwitch
- Text
- Textarea

### 4.2 Layouts

The Layouts collection provides components for composing page and application structures.

```tsx
import {
  AppLayout,
  Center,
  Cluster,
  Container,
  Forbidden,
  InternalServerError,
  NotFound,
  Grid,
  Reel,
  Stack,
} from '@noemaru1011/ui';
```

Available components:

- AppLayout
- Center
- Cluster
- Container
- Forbidden
- InternalServerError
- NotFound
- Grid
- Reel
- Stack

### 4.4 Primitive Components

Low-level UI primitives are available through the `primitives` namespace.

```tsx
import { primitives } from '@noemaru1011/ui';
```

The namespace exposes the components exported from `src/components/ui`.

These include:

- accordion
- alert
- alert-dialog
- badge
- breadcrumb
- button
- calendar
- card
- carousel
- checkbox
- combobox
- dialog
- drawer
- field
- input-group
- input
- label
- pagination
- popover
- radio-group
- select
- separator
- spinner
- switch
- table
- tabs
- textarea
- toast
- tooltip

Use the higher-level Elements and Layouts exports when they satisfy the use case. Use primitives when lower-level control is needed.

### 4.5 Other Exports

The package entry point also exports:

- Theme Provider
- i18n configuration
- data-table-features
- utility functions

Refer to `src/index.ts` and the corresponding source files for exact export names and signatures.

## 5. Button

The Button component is based on Base UI and uses class-variance-authority for variant and size styling.

### Variants

- `default`
- `outline`
- `secondary`
- `ghost`
- `destructive`
- `link`

### Sizes

- `default`
- `xs`
- `sm`
- `lg`
- `icon`
- `icon-xs`
- `icon-sm`
- `icon-lg`

### Loading State

The Button supports a `loading` property.

When loading is enabled:

- The button is disabled.
- `aria-busy` is set.
- A Spinner is displayed.

Example:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@noemaru1011/ui';

export function SaveButton() {
  return (
    <Button loading>
      Saving...
    </Button>
  );
}
```

The exact TypeScript interface should be checked in the published type definitions.

## 6. Styling and Theme

The library stylesheet is defined in:

- `src/index.css`

The project uses Tailwind CSS 4 and semantic CSS variables.

### Theme

The stylesheet defines:

- Light theme variables on `:root`
- Dark theme variables on `.dark`

The library supports semantic design tokens for colors and UI styling.

Use the provided theme variables rather than hardcoding colors when extending the design system.

### Typography

The stylesheet includes Noto Sans JP Variable as a Japanese font resource.

### Border Radius

The base radius is:

```css
--radius: 0.625rem;
```

This corresponds to 10px when the root font size is 16px.

The design system generally uses the standard radius scale. Documented exceptions include:

- `rounded-full`
- `rounded-none`
- `rounded-[inherit]`
- `rounded-[2px]`

### Z-index

The stylesheet defines semantic z-index utility classes:

- `z-base`
- `z-local`
- `z-sticky`
- `z-popover`
- `z-overlay`
- `z-modal`
- `z-toast`
- `z-tooltip`

Prefer these semantic layers when implementing overlays, dialogs, popovers, notifications, and tooltips.

## 7. Internationalization (i18n)

The i18n configuration is defined in:

- `src/i18n/index.ts`

The library uses:

- i18next
- i18next-browser-languagedetector
- react-i18next

Configuration:

- Default language: Japanese (`ja`)
- Fallback language: Japanese (`ja`)
- Default namespace: `common`
- Namespaces:
  - `common`
  - `error`
  - `example`

Language detection:

- localStorage
- Browser navigator

Detected language settings are cached in localStorage.

Refer to the i18n source and exported API for the exact initialization and integration procedure.

## 8. Basic Usage

```tsx
import '@noemaru1011/ui/style.css';

import {
  Button,
  Card,
  Heading,
  Stack,
  Text,
} from '@noemaru1011/ui';

export function SamplePage() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Card>
        <Heading>Welcome</Heading>
        <Text>This is a sample page.</Text>
        <Button>Continue</Button>
      </Card>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

This example illustrates the import pattern. Check the published type definitions for the exact props supported by each component.

## 9. Build and Source Structure

The library build configuration is:

- `vite.lib.config.ts`

The build entry point is:

- `src/index.ts`

The build output directory is:

- `dist`

The library build also generates TypeScript declaration files.

Important source locations:

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/index.ts` | Public package entry point |
| `src/components/elements/` | Higher-level reusable components |
| `src/components/layouts/` | Layout components |
| `src/components/ui/` | Low-level UI primitives |
| `src/components/providers/theme-provider/` | Theme provider |
| `src/i18n/` | Internationalization |
| `src/index.css` | Global styles and design tokens |
| `src/stories/` | Storybook documentation and examples |
| `.storybook/` | Storybook configuration |

## 10. Storybook

Storybook is used to document and demonstrate components.

Public Storybook:

https://noemaru1011.github.io/my-ui-catalog/

The project configures Storybook to load MDX and component stories from `src`.

Use Storybook to inspect component appearance and examples. For exact TypeScript APIs, use the source code or published declaration files.

## 11. Guidelines for AI Agents

When generating code using this library, follow these rules:

1. Import components from `@noemaru1011/ui` unless there is a clear reason to use another entry point.
2. Import `@noemaru1011/ui/style.css` in the application.
3. Prefer Elements and Layouts for common application UI.
4. Use `primitives` for low-level UI composition.
5. Do not invent component names, props, variants, or event handlers.
6. Verify exact component interfaces against the published TypeScript declaration files.
7. Do not assume every primitive has the same API as its higher-level counterpart.
8. Reuse the library's theme tokens and semantic styles.
9. Prefer the existing i18n configuration for translated text.
10. Use Storybook as a visual reference, not as a replacement for TypeScript API definitions.

## 12. Source of Truth

When information conflicts, use this priority order:

1. Published TypeScript declaration files

3. Package metadata
4. Storybook examples
5. README and other documentation
6. This AI context document

This document is intended to help AI systems understand the package structure and usage. It is not a replacement for the actual API definitions.
